دَخِنٌ [applied to food, and to flesh-meat, Infected with smoke: see دَخِنَ. ―
-b2- And hence,] applied to wine, or beverage, (assumed tropical:) Altered for the worse in odour. (TA.) ―
-b3- And رَجُلٌ دَخِنُ الخُلُقِ (Sh, JK, S) (tropical:) A man bad, corrupt, or wicked, in respect of nature, or disposition. (Sh, JK, TA.) [See also دَاخِنٌ.]
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
